Initial Assessment: Obtain comprehensive medical history, with attention to geographic origin (notably Asia, Native America, North Africa) and risk factors (tobacco, alcohol, EBV exposure). 2. Symptom Evaluation: Assess for enlarged lymph nodes, hearing loss, and other head and neck symptoms, noting that early NPC may be asymptomatic. 3. Diagnostic Workup: Perform physical examination and imaging studies (CT, MRI, PET/CT, ultrasound) to evaluate tumor extent and nodal involvement. 4. Histopathologic Confirmation: Conduct biopsy of nasopharyngeal lesion and/or lymph node (FNA, FNB, or CNB) to confirm diagnosis and determine subtype (e.g., SCC). 5. Biomarker Testing: Test for EBV DNA, MSI-H/dMMR, PD-L1, HPV, and tumor mutational burden at diagnosis. 6. Staging: Utilize the AJCC TNM system to classify tumor size, nodal involvement, and distant metastasis; categorize as resectable, unresectable, locoregional, locally advanced, or metastatic. 7. Multidisciplinary Review: Assess performance status, dental and nutritional health, and discuss fertility preservation when appropriate. 8. Surveillance: Plan follow-up with periodic imaging (CT, MRI, PET/CT) and serial EBV DNA testing post-treatment.
